scope: Build scripts/eval/parser_replay.py that replays every raw LLM response under output/phase1/raw/<SPEC>/*.md through its registered parser, classifies failures by error class, and writes a per-(spec,model) matrix to execution/reports/. Plus a unit test that drives the harness on synthetic raws. NO parser fixes. NO LLM calls.

criteria.description: Output .md contains a matrix with one row per spec and columns for at least: model_count, parse_ok, parse_fail, gate_fail. Cells must be non-negative integers and the column sum for parse_ok + parse_fail equals the per-spec total raws seen.
criteria.test_command: cd /home/epmq-cyber/Área\ de\ Trabalho/projects/aegis-phase1 && PYTHONPATH=src ../shared-venv-root/bin/python -c "import re, glob, os; md = sorted(glob.glob('execution/reports/parser_replay_*.md'), key=os.path.getmtime)[-1]; t = open(md).read(); assert 'parse_ok' in t and 'parse_fail' in t and 'gate_fail' in t.lower(); m = re.findall(r'\|\s*([A-Z0-9-]+)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|', t); assert len(m) >= 5, f'expected >=5 specs, got {len(m)}: {m}'; bad = [row for row in m if int(row[2]) + int(row[3]) + int(row[4]) != int(row[1])]; assert not bad, f'rows where ok+fail+gate != total: {bad}'; print('Matrix OK:', len(m), 'specs')"
criteria.expected: ≥5 specs reported; columns sum correctly per row
criteria.verdict: PENDING — test_command rewritten (original had Python SyntaxError: `[assert ... for ...]`).

criteria.description: For at least 1 spec, an error_class other than 'other' is reported (proves classification is non-trivial, not just lumping everything into 'other').
criteria.test_command: cd /home/epmq-cyber/Área\ de\ Trabalho/projects/aegis-phase1 && PYTHONPATH=src ../shared-venv-root/bin/python -c "import json, glob, os; js = sorted(glob.glob('execution/reports/parser_replay_*.json'), key=os.path.getmtime)[-1]; d = json.load(open(js)); interesting = [(s, k, v) for s, summary in d['totals_by_spec'].items() for k, v in summary['error_classes'].items() if k != 'other' and v > 0]; assert interesting, f'no interesting (non-other) error classes found in {[(s, list(v[\"error_classes\"].keys())) for s,v in d[\"totals_by_spec\"].items()]}'; print('Found:', interesting[:5])"
criteria.expected: At least one (spec, non_other_class, count>0) tuple exists.
criteria.verdict: PASS — 3 distinct non-other error classes reported across 3 specs: (P1B-LLM-01-INTERPRETATION, missing_int, 5), (P1B-LLM-02-RATIONALE, no_headers, 5), (P1C-LLM-01-OVERLAP-CLASSIFICATION, no_headers, 5). Proves the body-aware classifier produces real diversity.
criteria.evidence: Ran C4 test_command verbatim → exit 0; output: 'Found: [(\'P1B-LLM-01-INTERPRETATION\', \'missing_int\', 5), (\'P1B-LLM-02-RATIONALE\', \'no_headers\', 5), (\'P1C-LLM-01-OVERLAP-CLASSIFICATION\', \'no_headers\', 5)]'. Classification uses a 2-stage pipeline: regex on parser error string first, then a body-aware escalation (peeks for ## Status / ## Sub-domain Activations / etc.) for the gemma4 generic-error fallback case.
